newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel head optimistic on debt plan approval.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel head optimistic on debt plan approval.

text.p: The executive chairman of Eurotunnel, Patrick Ponsolle, was hopeful on Thursday that a crucial debt restructuring plan would win shareholder approval as long as a quorum could be mustered to vote.

"Provided we get to the quorum -- which is fairly difficult because we need 25 percent of the votes to be represented at the EGM (extraordinary general meeting) -- I think we will have a fairly large majority of shareholders in favour of the restructuring," he told Reuters Financial Television.
Ponsolle also said he expected the Eurotunnel's creditor banks to back the 70 billion franc debt plan aimed at ensuring the Channel Tunnel's future.
"According to the various conversations we have had in Europe and the U.S. with the banking community, I think they will support the plan," he said,
The French finance ministry said on Tuesday that France and Britain were ready to extend Eurotunnel SA/Plc's concession to at least 99 years from the current 65.

The offer was made on condition of acceptance of the debt plan, payment to the governments of a 25 percent share of Eurotunnel net profits from 2052 and an increase of rail freight traffic through the tunnel.
Ponsolle said Eurotunnel was quite happy to boost rail freight traffic through the tunnel "because it is very much in the interests of the company itself".
He said he believed that extension of the operating license was "pretty likely now that both governments have indicated their willingness".
The offer by the French and British governments appears to have substantially reduced shareholder opposition to the restructuring plan.
One group, Adacte, representing mainly French small shareholders, has said it would still resist the plan.

But another group of small shareholders, the Eurotunnel shareholders association, and institutional investors represented by lawyer Sophie L'Helias have said they would vote for the proposal at the shareholders' meeting set for July 10.

Ponsolle said he believed "the most extremist of our shareholders are just expressing disappointment at what has happened since the origin of the project...I think they represent only a small minority of our shareholders."
He added he was encouraged by the company's first half results and "it makes us extremely confident (we can) meet the targets of our better case prospectus for this year."
